c_sensitivity.record_shares_are_of_the_explained_38pct: record's 'ranks 1+2 carry 92.31% of the variance' is 92.31% of the 37.9% the linear model explains = ~35% of total variance.
c_sensitivity.un_attenuated_reranking: regressing EACH GATE separately (per-gate multivariate R2 median 0.9770, range 0.8304-0.9987) and pooling: cellN 73.24%, cellP 23.19%, park 1.49%, swP 1.09%, swN 0.98%.
c_sensitivity.this_VINDICATES_the_prereg_prediction: record scored its own prediction (cellN 81.7% / cellP 18.3%) as WRONG against its measured 52.42/39.89. Un-attenuated the measurement is 73.24/23.19 - CLOSE to the prediction. The record's self-criticism was itself an artefact of the min-statistic; it under-credited its own model.
c_sensitivity.swP_rank: record puts transfer pMOS 3rd (4.55%) and scores its 'ranks LAST' prediction as WRONG. Un-attenuated it is 4th of 5 (1.09%), i.e. nearly last. The record's finding that XSWP4 has the largest per-mV leverage (dM/dVt = -1.1834, 3-5x a cell device) is CONFIRMED and is the durable part.
c_sensitivity.DUT_B_ranking_CONTAMINATED: rx6.py line 128-129 builds the response as the mean over 8 lanes of the sign-corrected margin. 4 HIGH lanes FAIL at -114 to -117 mV; 4 LOW lanes pass at +393 to +398 mV. The mean is +140.133 mV - POSITIVE while 30/30 samples FAIL. This is the SAME near-cancellation the record caught for the receiver output (AMENDMENT A10 #3) and did not catch here.
c_sensitivity.DUT_B_corrected: re-ranked on the binding (HIGH-lane) half: cellP 37.24% RANK 1, cellN 29.95% rank 2 - the record's top two are INVERTED. rxSkewP_0u15 moves rank 8 (3.67%) -> rank 5 (5.23%), so the prereg 'rank 1' prediction is still refuted, but by less than reported and the multiplicity explanation survives.

polarity.census_reproduces_exactly: OPEN instant: pull-UP 3694/3900 = 94.72%, pull-DOWN 0/3300 = 0.00%. BOUND instant: 0/3900 and 0/3300. Counts 3900=13 HIGH gates x300 and 3300=11 LOW x300 confirmed.
polarity.overstated_one_sidedness: 'every failure is a pull-up shortfall / there is no other half' is literally true but all those failures are at the OPEN instant, which the record itself rejects as its criterion (300/300 nominal fail). At the PRIMARY bound instant there are no failures to classify.
polarity.regime_switch_within_the_chain: the record quotes pull-down at 137-474 sigma. That holds only for links 1->2 and 3->4, where LOW outputs are fully discharged (0.0047 V and -0.0034 V, sd 0.5-2.3 mV). At link 2->3 the LOW outputs sit at 43-46 mV, NOT ground, with sd 14.6-17.3 mV -> 18.46-22.05 sigma. That is the SECOND-tightest regime in the chain and it is the OPPOSITE polarity, only 1.39x looser than the tightest pull-up (13.24 sigma). A pMOS-only sizing fix would push it to binding.

e_cost.level_time_reproduces: 138.065/127.637/135.802/169.901 ps for base/Wx2/Wx4/Lx2 - matches the record to the digit. Slack 61.935/72.363/64.198/30.099 ps likewise.
e_cost.MISSING_AXIS_nominal_margin: the record's cost axes were yield/area/level-time/C-proxy. It never reported what resizing does to the NOMINAL margin: base 262.97 mV -> Wx2 268.25 (+2.0%) -> Wx4 206.19 (-21.6%) -> Lx2 107.62 (-59.1%).
e_cost.MISSING_AXIS_rail_amplitude: resizing LOADS the resonant rail: bank-2 rail 0.6767 -> 0.6153 (Wx2) -> 0.5481 (Wx4); Lx2 keeps 0.7040 but cell reach collapses 91.1% -> 66.7%. Two DISTINCT mechanisms: width costs rail amplitude and buys drive; length preserves the rail and destroys drive.
e_cost.equal_WL_is_NOT_equal_loading: Wx2 and Lx2 have identical W*L product and identical sigma, yet rails 0.6153 vs 0.7040. So rail droop is set by the CURRENT the cells draw, not by gate capacitance. An optimiser using C ~ W*L cannot see this.
e_cost.margin_in_sigma: base 20.9, Wx2 59.5, Wx4 19.5, Lx2 18.9 (nominal worst margin / mean pull-up gate sd). Wx2 is the ONLY variant that improves robustness; Wx4 and Lx2 are NO BETTER than base for +95.2% and +31.7% device area.
e_cost.AREA_DENOMINATOR_WRONG_BOUNDARY: the committed banktank row carries tank_area_um2_per_chain = 959.44 um2 (MIM 239.86 x 4 banks). Device area 24.3776 um2 is 2.48% of chain area. So Wx2's '+31.7%' is +0.79% of chain area and Wx4's '+95.2%' is +2.36%. The record flagged that 68.3% of its device area is park+transfer but never noted the tank dominates the real denominator. Area is essentially a non-cost for Wx2.
e_cost.turnover_evidence_too_weak_in_record: record's interior-optimum claim rests on 8.2 ps of level time (Wx2 72.363 vs Wx4 64.198 slack) - but the measurement grid step is 10.155-10.479 ps, so that gap is SUB-RESOLUTION. Chain slack is quantised to 2-3 distinct grid values per variant, and Wx2's link 3->4 is censored at the grid start in 50/50 samples. The record's '15.7 SE' / '86 SE' precision claims on slack are spurious. The W-vs-L gap (42.264 ps, ~4 grid steps) IS resolvable, so 'width beats length on time' stands.
e_cost.turnover_CONFIRMED_on_better_axes: the interior optimum at Wx2 is nonetheless real, on three axes I measured that the record did not use: nominal margin (+2.0% / -21.6% / -59.1%), margin-in-sigma (20.9/59.5/19.5/18.9), and the absolute boundary-receiver margin below.

sizing_x_receiver_interaction.the_record_treated_these_as_independent: Rule 5 (skewed receiver, 0/300 vs 191/300) was measured only at BASE geometry; Phase 2 recommends resizing. Resizing changes the absolute level, and an absolute trip does not scale with the rail.
findings: RX_SKEW survives every geometry (0/50 everywhere) - Rule 5 is robust to sizing, which the record asserted but never tested.
RX_STD base fails 29/50 = 58%, independently replicating the headline 191/300 = 63.7% at a different seed and N.
Wx2 nearly RESCUES the standard receiver: 29/50 -> 2/50. That is a new result and it is the strongest single argument for Wx2 - it could remove the need for a skewed boundary cell.
Wx4 and Lx2 take bank 4 BELOW the standard trip outright (-114.24 and -88.23 mV, 50/50) and halve the skewed-receiver margin. Upsizing past Wx2 forfeits the boundary margin Rule 5 depends on.

dut_b.deterministic_failure_confirmed: bank 6 HIGH class 0.34406 V vs the 0.4595 V trip = -115.44 mV, 30/30, and at zero mismatch. Class separation 280.27 mV CONFIRMED exactly (record's figure).
dut_b.bank5_562mV_is_a_CONFLATION: record says 'bank 5 clears 0.4595 V with 562 mV'. 561.41 mV is bank 5's CLASS SEPARATION. Its actual margin above the trip is +99.69 mV (worst lane +98.93 mV, sd 6-7 mV, ~15 sigma). The placement recommendation SURVIVES but the quoted headroom is overstated 5.6x.
dut_b.per_bank_decline_measured: margin of the worst HIGH lane vs 0.4595 V: bank2 +589.69 (208 sigma), bank3 +419.72 (301), bank4 +260.40 (258), bank5 +92.22 (21.3), bank6 -128.32 (FAIL 30/30)

bounds_confirmed: tt corner / nominal temperature only - not PVT sign-off
delvto only; PDK also carries factuo_mm 0.005/0.0033, dw_mm 4e-9, dl_mm 2e-9 -> every sigma a LOWER bound, every margin-in-sigma an UPPER bound
ad=as=pd=ps=0 in the shim -> zero junction capacitance, both the load and its own mismatch absent, yields are UPPER bounds
junction cap scales with W, so it bites the WIDTH variants' advantage hardest: the direction of the Wx2 recommendation is robust, the location of the optimum is not and can only move DOWN

energy not metered here (integrators dropped) - but the committed banktank row DOES carry per-bank energy (E_out_of_tank_rise 34-39 fJ, recycle 9.6-22%), so a Phase-2 energy cost was obtainable by re-running the 4 variants with integrators. Not done.
measures are taken at 601/801/1001 ps while the committed boundary is 600/800/1000 ps - 1 ps late, negligible against ~62 ps of slack, but it is 1 ps of extra settling

depth_accumulation_claim.record_claim: 'mismatch variance ACCUMULATES with depth: pull-up margin sd 7.3-8.1 mV at link 1->2 vs 19.6-22.7 mV at link 3->4', used as reason (iii) to expect the bar to tighten
depth_accumulation_claim.reading: pull-up sd is FLAT link1->link2 then x2.8 at link3; pull-down sd PEAKS at the middle link. The pull-down excursion tracks bank 3's LOW outputs failing to reach ground (44.7 mV vs 4.7 and -3.5 mV), and bank 3 carries the COMPLEMENT of the pattern at banks 2 and 4. What is measured is bank-to-bank alternation tied to the test pattern, NOT monotone accumulation with depth. The 'deeper datapath is worse' extrapolation is a two-point over-read.
depth_accumulation_claim.also: bank 1's inputs are ideal sources (VI1_0..7), so only 3 of the 4 banks are real-driven; the scored depth is 3 stages / 24 gates, which the record does state as 24 links

no_unit_bug: verified independently: all 76 devices in bt_mc_2001.cir.meta.json parse from /usr/local/src/stat-sim/qal/banktank/c_m10_T200_H4_dv1200_free.cir with 0 mismatches; class census 32 cellP / 32 cellN / 4 swN / 4 swP / 4 park = 76 matches the pre-registered census; every sigma re-derives from the PDK A_VT to <1e-6 mV; area recomputes 24.3776 um2
my_own_process_errors: I launched two Xyce jobs concurrently that hashed to the SAME PyMS .so path; they raced on a shared .so.build/ scratch dir and produced a C++ codegen error (d_zg__sel6_dS undeclared), then a silent fallback to a REDUCED model (376 params, nonzero-only) where every one of the study's own builds was (782 params, full). Caught by diffing my build banner against theirs. Fixed by serialising with per-run PYMS_VAE_CACHE dirs. NOTE: this is a real hazard for the study too - it ran 3 same-geometry chunks concurrently against one cache and got full builds only by timing luck.

My first .prn parser assumed one 'Index' header per .step block; Xyce emits ONE header and restarts the index. Caught because the cross-term matrix came back empty rather than wrong - re-split on the index reset.
